usageNotes: Use this to read the current firewall behavior settings for a specific QEMU VM — including whether the firewall is enabled, default input/output policies, DHCP/NDP/MAC filter state, and log levels. Requires VM.Audit on the VM's path; no node-level privilege is needed. If the firewall has never been explicitly configured for the VM, most fields will be absent (falling back to their documented defaults).

examples.summary: Retrieve firewall options for VM 105 on node pve1

tips: Fields not returned in the response are at their default values (e.g. enable defaults to false, macfilter defaults to true).
A VM firewall being enabled here does not mean rules exist — check the rules endpoint separately to confirm active rule coverage.
policy_in and policy_out are only meaningful when the firewall is enabled; the default implicit policy when no policy is set is ACCEPT.
ipfilter, when enabled, auto-populates per-interface ipsets with link-local restrictions — useful for preventing IP spoofing without manual ipset management.
